extracted.intended_audience: prospective Hertz Fellowship applicants (doctoral students) and their recommenders
extracted.subtask_description: Information and implicit selection criteria for applicants to the Hertz Fellowship, a competitive doctoral fellowship for students in applied sciences, engineering, and mathematics. Describes who can apply, the program's priorities (innovation, interdisciplinarity, impact), and the role of recommenders and community support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: doctoral students in applied sciences, engineering, and mathematics
rubrics_metrics.description: The Hertz Fellowship provides financial and lifelong professional support for the nation’s most promising doctoral students in the applied sciences, engineering and mathematics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should be doctoral students (or entering doctoral study) in applied sciences, engineering, or mathematics. The program is targeted to this disciplinary scope; other fields are not emphasized on this page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary merit: 'most promising innovators'
rubrics_metrics.description: Empowering the most promising innovators; the Hertz Fellowship provides support for the nation’s most promising talent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection prioritizes individuals judged to be 'most promising' — i.e., those who demonstrate exceptional potential for innovation and scientific/technical leadership. The page emphasizes promise over rote metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problem focus: tackling challenging and interdisciplinary problems
rubrics_metrics.description: “We’re interested in individuals tackling challenging questions in their fields, but also determined to solve big interdisciplinary problems facing the nation and the world.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should demonstrate engagement with hard technical questions in their discipline and motivation/ability to address large interdisciplinary problems with societal or national significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversity of disciplines and backgrounds
rubrics_metrics.description: The nation’s most promising talent comes from different disciplines, backgrounds, and points of view.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program values intellectual and demographic diversity; reviewers are encouraged to consider diverse disciplinary perspectives and backgrounds when assessing applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation letters: role of recommenders from academia and industry
rubrics_metrics.description: Our recommenders in academia and industry are integral in helping students apply for the Hertz Fellowship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High-quality recommendations (from academic and/or industry referees) are an important component of a competitive application. The page provides a dedicated resources link for recommenders, implying expectations for thoughtful, informed letters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential for impact and leadership
rubrics_metrics.description: From the moment the Hertz Fellowship is awarded, it changes the trajectory of a life — and often, the course of science itself. (Examples: advising presidents, coaching Olympiad teams, developing tests for fake drugs, founding companies.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should demonstrate or project potential for substantial impact in their field or society, and capacity for leadership (research leadership, public-facing impact, entrepreneurship, policy influence, etc.). Past Fellows’ stories are used as exemplars.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitment to community, collaboration, and mentorship
rubrics_metrics.description: Hertz Fellows find common ground in curiosity, creativity, and mutual respect — leading to collaborations that cross disciplines. Fellows also work with a dedicated mentor throughout their fellowship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants who show willingness and ability to participate in a collaborative community and to benefit from/engage in mentoring relationships align with program values; interpersonal and collaborative qualities are relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fit with program's 'Freedom to Innovate' value (research independence and flexibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: As a Hertz Fellow, you gain the Freedom to Innovate® ... This flexibility enables you to secure your top choice in advisor and research group, explore ideas outside the constraints of an advisor’s grants, develop collaborative projects and reduce distractions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While a program benefit, this implies selection of candidates who will make productive, independent use of flexible support — i.e., those who benefit from research independence and are likely to pursue high-risk/high-reward or cross-disciplinary work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selectivity and longevity of support
rubrics_metrics.description: Awarded through a rigorous selection process honed over seven decades; Hertz Fellows receive up to five years of funding and join an influential community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The fellowship is highly selective and intended as multi-year investment; reviewers look for applicants for whom multi-year support is justified by promise and projected trajectory.
